text:
incident-bot: Paging @sre-oncall — KV cache block-manager reporting abnormal page allocations on runtime-prod. Memory pressure + continuous-batching spike. Alert: mem > 88% on shard-gpu-12, 95th latency x3. Detected 11:02:27 UTC.

sre-oncall: on it. what's the customer impact? any 5xxs or timed out requests?

maria: I'm seeing increased tail latencies on /v1/generate across multiple regions, some requests are timing out at 30s. Dashboard shows batching queue depth jumping and KV eviction rate spiking.

aj: alerted support — analyzing error rates now. Early estimate: ~4-6% of hosted traffic experiences >5s latency, 0.8% 500s.

olivia: stack traces from node shard-gpu-12 show block manager thrashing: frequent small allocations and meta lookups. suspect block size tuning plus eviction policy regression after last runtime bump.

tyler: I rolled the latest continuous-batching changes yesterday — included block-manager metadata caching change (PR #4891). Could be related.

ryan: grabbing logs. sample from 11:03:13 UTC:
```
[block-manager] alloc_page(size=65536) -> created page_id=0x7f9a1b
[evict] evict_page(page_id=0x7f9a1b) -> moved to cold, metadata leak: handle_count still 2
[batch] enqueue batch_id=2987 size=78 tokens
[latency] request_id=... p95=3.1s
```

maria: looks like a metadata leak — handle_count not zero after evict, causing page reuse to stall and allocation churn. When allocation fails, continuous batching falls back to smaller batches -> perf cliff.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options? can we throttle batching or force eviction policy to aggressive?

tyler: we can hotfix config to reduce max_batch_tokens and disable the new metadata caching flag. Hotfix proposal:
- set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096 -> currently 65536
- set BLOCK_META_CACHE=false
- restart block-manager service on affected shards one at a time

aj: +1. That should reduce allocation pressure quickly. Rolling restart plan? we need zero-downtime.

olivia: do not restart whole node, restart block-manager process inside runtime container. We have graceful handoff support. Steps:
1) drain new requests to target runtime instance (scale down by weight)
2) restart block-manager 
3) validate mem and p95 for 3 minutes
4) bring back weight

sre-oncall: executing hotfix now. tagging infra-bot for config change.

infra-bot: config update accepted: CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096; BLOCK_META_CACHE=false. Applying to runtime-prod group shards [10..14] with 30s stagger.

(2m)

maria: first shard restart in progress (shard-gpu-10). Draining at 11:08 UTC.

(5m)

ryan: shard-gpu-10 block-manager restarted. mem usage dropped from 91% -> 72% on that host. p95 reduced from 3.2s -> 0.9s for that shard.

olivia: progress check: after first two shards hotfixed, overall cluster p95 down ~45%, timeouts gone for traffic hitting those shards. Still higher on shards 12-14.

tyler: leaving a quick revert PR for the metadata caching change: revert PR #4891 -> draft revert queued if hotfix doesn't fully resolve.

(12m)

aj: notifying support & customer success. Customer impact summary: small subset of streaming customers in EU experienced elevated latency and a few mid-tier customers saw degraded throughput. No data corruption reported. We opened internal incidents for affected accounts and offered degrade-mitigation suggestions.

sre-oncall: continuing rolling restarts. ETA to finish remaining shards 15 minutes. After hotfix we'll run smoke tests for embedding and generate endpoints.

infra-bot: all target shards updated with new config. Restarts completed at 11:27 UTC.

maria: cluster-wide mem pressure normalized. p95 now within SLO. Continuous-batching queue depth stable. Eviction rate back to baseline.

lena: can we capture core dump / extra traces from block-manager for later root-cause? request snapshot from affected shards before GC purges metadata.

ryan: grabbed debug snapshots (metadata maps, handle tables) and uploaded to secure storage. Links: https://internal/coredumps/1763381247-snapshots (access: infra/read).

tyler: follow-up action items:
- revert or fix block-manager metadata caching (PR review)
- add guardrails for handle_count mismatches -> assert/metrics
- add auto-throttle for CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS when mem>80%
- postmortem with timeline and customer impact

aj: scheduling on-call handoff notes into tomorrow's shift. Assigning postmortem owner: @maria.

maria: will own PM. Tentative postmortem outline: timeline, root cause (metadata leak + batch size), mitigations (hotfix, config guardrails), customer impact, long-term fix (rework caching + tune block size and eviction), monitoring changes.

sre-oncall: handing off to next oncall @lena at 11:45 UTC — cluster stable but continue to monitor. Please escalate if any regression.

lena: acknowledged. I'll keep watch and follow up with PM for notice to affected customers.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (hotfix applied, rolling restarts completed). Severity: Sev2 -> Root cause investigation in progress.

maria: quick note for postmortem: also consider block-size experiment matrix (64k vs 32k vs 128k) and eviction policy (LRU vs generational). We'll run canary tests against synthetic load.

tyler: logging lesson: add per-page handle_count histogram to metrics so we can alert before leak causes thrash.

aj: closing loop with support — customers informed, offers for additional capacity if needed.

lena: thanks everyone. I'll post the incident blameless timeline and link to snapshots in #postmortems when PM draft ready.

(End of thread)
